text:
Sasha: noticing weird kernel routing on a handful of prod hosts after the node-driver update. some GPUs are being routed to the slow fp32 path even though they have tensor cores and bf16 advertised.
Divya: hmm. is this the probe that uses NVML feature bits or our pci_device_id table?
Sasha: our probe prefers nvml feature flags first, then sm_version. after 545 driver the NVML reports "mathMode=0" intermittently. looks like a race or nvml query timeout.
Matt: pasting a small dump from one affected host (anonymized):
```
$ sudo ./nvml_probe.py --json
{"pci_id": "10de:2484", "sm": "8.6", "tensor_cores": true, "bf16": true, "nvml_math_mode": 0, "driver": "545.23"}
```
Sasha: that matches. pci id says Ampere, sm 86, but nvml_math_mode=0. our kernel-selector currently: prefer nvml_math_mode -> tensor_core flag -> sm version -> microbench.
Divya: we should invert probe ordering. fall back to pci id/compute capability if NVML is flaky. also add a microbench step that runs a tiny 1-2iter kernel probe (very short) to confirm fp8/bf16 kernels available before routing.
InfraBot: automated-probe results (2773334452): 12 hosts flagged. suggestion: add config toggle `probe_strictness` to gate microbench.
Sasha: noted. also seeing KV-cache churn on those hosts when fallback switches kernels mid-run — prefetch logic expects stable kernel path. when kernel path flips we end up copying/evicting lots of KV entries.
Matt: example perf microbenchmark (local lab, seq-len sweep):
```
seq=64  -> fastpath (TC) 4.2ms  fallback (FP32) 5.1ms
seq=128 -> fastpath (TC) 9.9ms  fallback (FP32) 10.1ms
seq=512 -> fastpath (TC) 38.6ms fallback (FP32) 34.2ms  <-- surprising: FP32 wins at long seq on this driver
```
Divya: that last line is the regression. might be a driver shader scheduling change. either adjust kernel pick rules to be sequence-length-aware (choose FP32 for seq>256 on that driver) or pin kernels per node after a stable probe.
Sasha: prefer pin-per-host after at most N probes. also add a sticky-tag on KV entries w/ kernel-path hash so we don't evict when hash flips temporarily.
Matt: proposed config snippet to add to runtime autotune: 
```
autotune:
  gpu_probe:
    probe_order: [pci_device_id, sm_version, nvml_features, microbench]
    microbench_budget_ms: 20
    sticky_kernel_pin_seconds: 3600
    sequence_len_overrides:
      ">=256": "prefer_fp32"
```
Divya: +1. tests needed: driver 545 and 550, multiple samples on same host across reboots. add a short canary job to watchdog for kernel flips.
InfraBot: created ticket INF-7219 and scheduled canary run in staging for 03/29.
Sasha: action items: (1) implement probe_order change + microbench (2) add sticky kernel-tag to KV cache metadata (3) add canary and metrics for kernel_flip_count. I'll draft the PR today and tag @Matt and @Divya for review. :thumbsup:
Matt: thanks. i'll prepare a small microbench harness and add a test vector for seq=512 oddity.
Divya: i'll own the canary + dashboards. if we see >0.5 flips/hour we revert routing to pci-id only.
Sasha: cool. pushing a tiny diagnostic patch to trace probe decisions now, will post link when ready.
